[quote=aceldix;60926310][spoiler=[b]Incident at Whitney[/b]]

[b]Five miles north of Whitney, Province of Whitney[/b]

Upon receiving reports from the Hamilton Radar Station of the situation in the skies, the surrounding provinces perked up their atmospheric defenses to deal with the threat. However, upon witnessing the ship release a shuttle onto the moon, the unfolding events concerning the spacecraft gave attention to the military, who were now very intrigued in the unfolding situation. While unable to prevent the shuttle from reaching Aceldama, the radar stations were able to observe and pinpoint its trajectory and landing location, determining that it was headed for Whitney, a city easily visible from outer space.

~ ~ ~

The entrance of Frame 167 came sudden and quick, shooting down through the air at breakneck speed. When Frame 167 hit the earth, it conjured a powerful force in the ground, sending dust flying and rocks tumbling over, of which there were no witnesses to marvel. Upon landing, the mech slowly stood back up and looked straight, back facing the bright rays of the Sun. The driver within quickly paused to inspect his mech for damage. Once concluding that everything worked fine, Frame 167 turned on its boosters and began to hover around the badlands of Aceldama for signs of human settlement.

It didnt take very long. About 20 minutes into the operation, Frame 167 spotted about a dozen buildings in the distance. Upon inspection, it appeared to be a mining facility, laden with humans, robots and valuable infrastructure alike. Frame 167 saw no trace of military activity within the mining encampment, nor any defensible positions within the facility. A stunning target indeed, it thought. The mechs boosters flared with power and its plasma rifle was armed in preparation.

~ ~ ~

The miners never saw it coming. A few crewmen reported seeing something odd in the distance, but they were not nearly as calculating nor caring as the men in Hamilton Radar Station. And then, all of a sudden, a metal object- no, machine- was zooming towards the facility. A number of brave souls ran to ring the alarm, but it was too late. Within seconds, the giant mech, oddly with no markings for identification, began firing upon the encampment. A few valiant miners threw their wrenches and shovels at the mech, but these were scratches, if even, on the mech. The mech hoisted its shield and rammed it against a building, bursting through its walls and wreaking havoc upon the unsuspecting facility.

Luckily, for the inhabitants of the mining community, Aceldix had been watching over them, and had guessed with solid accuracy where the shuttle from earlier had landed. The mech, in a rampage to try out its polished rocket launchers, saw out of the corner of its eye a large, dark figure in the sky. It suddenly hit her: retribution was quickly approaching. She thus made it her goal to cause as much destruction as possible; just follow the orders, use everything in the arsenal. Minutes later, help arrived in the form of tanks and armored cars. 

Aceldix drew first blood, as a tank fired an explosive shell at the mech. Frame 167 quickly raised her shield, blocking the attack but staggering her in the process; she had reacted too fast and without confidence behind her step. Frame 167 wasted no time, as she fired rocket launchers at the armored battalion. This mech was armed to the teeth, the Aceldixans thought. Whose robot is this? Battle soon raged on, between the mysterious mech from the unnamed carrier and the defensive forces of Aceldix.

Much time passed, and Frame 167 was beginning to take heavy damage. The Aceldixans were much more numerous in number than previously thought. In the goal to cause as much damage as possible, Frame 167 launched a salvo of rockets from her shoulders before turning 180 degrees and attempting an escape from the ground-based vehicles. One of the tanks would fire a desperate shot at the mech to try and prevent its escape.

Lucky hit. And a mighty one at that.

The mech suddenly saw its own arm mangled and critical systems within heavily damaged. The mech hit the ground at tremendous force, rattling the very earth around. The armored vehicles were initially very quiet before maneuvering out of the mining grounds and moving towards the mech. But upon reaching it, everything seemed off about it.

[/spoiler]
[nation]Orange Creek[/nation][/quote]
[b]15 January 2167

Operation Scoria I[/b]

The "battle", if you could even call it that, was brief. No more than a few minutes after the mobile suit had been dropped from the sky, Frame 167 had already expended most of its arsenal.  But this had already been planned beforehand. No military technology on Ardagan was capable of surviving fighting alone, especially not experimental prototypes with its multitude of unknowns. And yet, even as Frame 167 fell to the ground hard, it lay in the great field of blood of its own creation.

In the few minutes in between its initial landing and now, the mobile suit had caused immense casualties. Entire habitats would be pierced wide open, the protective shells preserving their artificlal atmospheres split wide open by an awesome barrage of plasma and rocket fire. Concrete structures would be blown apart, the water in their closed cavities instantly vaporized by plasma fire. Ballistic steel would be deformed into unrecognizable shapes or molten down completelely. Those directly hit would have simply ceased to exist, reduced into an amorphous, black ash and pungent viscera.

And yet, despite it all, the battle was not yet over. Deep in the cockpit of the mobile suit, NSI3-4 would survive the fall, protected by the mobile suit's own protective cockpit and her set of heavy power armor, which had been developed just for this purpose.

[list]"Reactor core's dead.. not a single limb's working anymore... tch..." NSI3-4 clicked her tongue as she aggressively attempted to interface with her mobile suit's internal computer to keep up the fight, though to no avail. Far too many critical components had been destroyed, first during that last hit, then in the fall.[/list]

The Aceldixan tank had scored an accurate hit near the mobile suit's thermonuclear fusion reactor, effectively killing its capacity to produce anymore energy, with deuterium-tritium fuel encased in the mobile suit's energy cells immediately vaporizing into Aceldama's paper-thin atmosphere in a brief but ominous, colorless haze. Without fusion energy to sustain itself, the mobile suit fell back on backup fuel systems to power only its most basic systems.

[list]"... Very well, I suppose this is it..." said the clone, sighing as she watched the Aceldixans close in, unstrapping herself from her seat. But she wasn't doing this in preparation for surrender and capture. SummitONE's orders, after all, were very explicit that not a single identifiable trace be salvaged from the attack.[/list]

Reaching for the computer one last time, NSI3-4 input a code into its operating software, which overrode several safety checks. It was a decisive "killswitch", preprogrammed into the frame's system for this very moment. As the Aceldixan's closed in on Frame 167, they would hear a strange, almost rhythmic humming, a strange bellowing sound, like the sound of a great drill quietly rising up from beneath the ground.

[list]"... Ha... I am signing out. Glory to the Kingdom!" the clone screamed out, and then was no more, as a gigantic blast would suddenly tear the mobile suit's cockpit wide open, igniting every single remaining fuel source embedded into the mobile suit along with all unexpended rockets and bombs, instantly shredding the mech and incinerating the clone and her armor into a mangled, unrecognizable substance.[/list]

Any crew that had been up close and personal would also be immediately obliterated by the blast, though the damage from the explosion would be ineffective beyond point-blank range. And, as the Aceldixans recuperated from this seemingly random last act of defiance, they would immediately come to realize that the pilot of the mech had apparently survived. Who, in their last moments, had decided to initiate a self-destruct sequence to obscure identifiable materials within the machine.

Armaments would be torn apart into junk, the suit's proprietary fusion reactor would be blown apart, while the cockpit would simply be gone. And yet, a mangled corpse of a mech still clearly, visibly remained. An arm and leg would be flown off from the explosion and strike the ground, badly damaged, but relatively intact, while the overall frame of the machine would still remain discernible from a glance, a sort of "spine" consisting of the various intersects and closed circuits that made up the mobile suit's source of mobility.

However, the most notable of all would be a small shard of plating, also expelled from the machine in the great blast. Perhaps it came from the mecha's shoulder armor, or on one of its armaments, or still maybe on the shuttle it had landed on. On that plating, apart from the pitch black color, was a strange, almost runic symbol, partially obscured by deformation and ash. It would be readily apparent to the Aceldixans then that the rune seemed to be of Elseyran character.

[b]Operation Scoria II

26 January 2167[/b]

After successfully dropping NSI3-4's mecha onto Aceldama, the [i]Kipsaga[/i] continued on to its next target: Hyperborea. According to League reports, an emergent power existed in Hyperborea in the form of the Ilynite Sovereignty, though its exact geopolitical capabilities remained the topic of speculation. In any case, the League had some cursory information of that country's defensive posturing and strong technological foundation relative to the League's own capabilities.

With the Aceldixan Confederacy having suffered great damage during the attack on Whitney, the [i]Kipsaga[/i] crew now hoped for the same to be inflicted sevenfold on the Illynites and accelerate the creation of a system-wide military-industrial complex.

[list]"But we can't be too hasty." cautioned Captain Voaden to the clone behind him, his eyes locked against the camera feed of deep space and the slowly forming view of venerable Hyperborea. "NSI3-4's mission had been a relative success, though she made herself too exposed too quickly. Straight up just threw herself to the wolves without any cover. NSI3-5, you're to follow the lessons learned from Aceldama and land dead center, are you confident in your ability to do so?"

"I am not." bluntly answered NSI3-5, her voice muffled by her huge gas mask. "I can certainly try to, however. Though, from the looks of things, Illynis's point defenses will be even stronger than Aceldix's."

"We fitted a ballute system into the shuttle for that purpose. We have zero faith that the landing shuttle will be able to survive, so we'll have to hope the ballute will help you land on Illynis with only a few scratches."

"And if I do not land safely?"

"Welp, sucks to be you. Anyways, ready? Illynis is fast approaching."

"Mhm."[/list]

With that quick brief, NSI3-5 headed towards the second landing shuttle embedded into the [i]Kipsaga[/i], and in that shuttle, the second Frame 167 to be used for Operation Scoria. As with Aceldama, the [i]Kipsaga[/i] rapidly approaching Illynis in a series of powerful nuclear pulses, the ship's pusher plate gliding the craft along towards its destination. To the Illynites, they would spot a strange object in the deep emptiness of space, a set of faint red "fins", in reality the ship's thermal radiators, emanating what little heat its minimally-stressed systems were emanating into deep space.

However, having learned its lesson from Aceldama, the [i]Kipsaga[/i] immediately activated its thrusters and made an about-face, at the same time shooting the second landing shuttle out of its compartment, the chemrockets of the shuttle flaring to life as it began its rapid, seemingly suicidal descent down into Illynis's dead atmosphere.

[b]Foe![/b]

The shuttle itself wasn't a particularly amazing contraption, its "hull" effectively just a gigantic sheet of titanium alloy folded over into the shape of a huge battery, with stabilizing fins that corrected the shuttle's descent and prevent it from tumbling down and landing on its ass. Around the shuttle, apart from a few exterior bipropellant fuel tanks, were four sets of chemical rockets that blasted methane fuel upwards as the shuttle fell to Illynis, slowing down the shuttle away from a thousand km/s to just a few hundred m/s in Illynis's virtually nonexistent atmosphere.

By the time Illynite defensive fire would manage to destroy the shuttle's frame, it was already too late. NSI3-5, pilot of the Frame 167 mobile suit ensconced within the shuttle, would momentarily consider bailing out with the ballute. However, after peeking out and watching the horrible salvo of munitions flying towards her way, NSI3-5 would opt to just stay within the destroyed frame of the shuttle a little longer for protection, grasping onto bits and pieces of titanium plating when she could as the shuttle hurtled towards the surface of the moon, staring out carefully until...

[i]BANG![/i]

With a quiet, almost noiseless burst, the shuttle is struck by a lucky strike from a Warden, at last obliterating the disable frame into smeltable junk. However, its presumed occupants were nowhere to be seen. NSI3-5 had jumped from the shuttle with her Frame 167 and propelled herself away just as the shuttle was destroyed. The mobile suit would still impact the ground at a dozen meters per second, causing the clone to momentarily wince from the shock.

[list]"Ugh... foot thrusters damaged, but apart from that, nothing seems off..." says NSI3-5, sighing as she briefly looked over her Frame 167's internal computer. Apart from a few anomalies, things seemed fine for now. "Very well, here goes nothing I suppose..."[/list]

The Frame 167 briefly looked around for a moment to check its surroundings. Before it were a network of domes, seemingly spaced perfectly apart, like polka dots fine table cloth. In the sky, two tiny specs were fast approaching, PT boats, rushing to investigate what had just crashed. Then, on the ground, tanks and what seemed to be humanoid constructs like the Frame 167, but on a smaller scale. NSI3-5 had been sufficiently warned of Illynis's military capabilities and would not waste this opportunity on engaging with the enemy's overwhelming firepower.

Mounting its shield on its back to keep itself safe, the Frame 167 turned away from the Illynite military response and began by opening fire on the surface colonies, its railgun firing a devastating barrage of 100mm tungsten penetrators to obliterate entire domes, blast open energy supplies, and instigate panic among the Illynite population. All the while, high-fragmentation rockets would be fired from the 167's shoulder-mounted launchers, creating a dense field of smog that fell slowly to Illynis's surface as a dense, sooty coating.

[b]Viral Clip on AnTube - Premier Arlan Vos meets Sultan Masud al-Ayyubi[/b]

[i]*Premier Vos seated beside Sultan Masud al-Ayyubi, Foreign Minister Abdoul Mahonomayi, and Defense Minister Musa al-Yahudiyyah in the Golden Office, answering the first press question about the meeting*
[/i]
Thank you, thank you, its wonderful, really wonderful, to have our friends from [nation]Baladullah[/nation] here today. Incredible people, very strong people. We had a meeting, a very big meeting, very important, and I can tell you, folks, it went fantastically well. Some of the best discussions weve had with any nation since the reunification. Everybodys saying it.
Sultan Masud, a tremendous leader, truly, came in with some really good ideas and plans. You know, not everybody has that anymore, in these days, yeah... And we talked about things that matter, like fighting terrorism, which Tirakan knows a lot about, believe me, defending sovereignty, and building prosperity across the Shamats. Very powerful topics, and were totally aligned. Totally.

The BTTA, amazing agreement. Very fair, very balanced, and it benefits both our nations. You dont see that often. No ridiculous tariffs, no nonsense, just straight, good business. Copper, steel, gas, we do them better than anyone, everybody knows it, and now our friends in Baladullah get to benefit too. And we get access to their industries in a way that works for everyone. People said it couldnt be done. Well, we did it.

And I want to say this clearly. Tirakan respects Baladullahs system, their culture, their values. Absolutely. Were not here to tell anyone how to run their country. Were here to make great deals, to build great partnerships, and were doing that. The Sultan talked about anti-colonialism, about self-determination, and let me tell you, nobody understands that better than us. Tirakan has rebuilt itself after thirty years of war. We know what sovereignty means. We know what strength means.
We agree completely that the Shamats, the whole region, is better when shamatine nations stand together. No foreign domination, no outsiders telling us what to do. Strong neighbors make a strong neighborhood. And with Baladullah, we have a chance to build something really historic, something very, very successful. I think its going to be one of the strongest partnerships on the continent. Maybe the strongest. People will be talking about this for a long time.

So I want to thank the Sultan, the Foreign Minister, the Defense Minister, incredible guys, for their honesty, their professionalism, and their friendship.
